description: Evaluation policy for the authoritative structural-worlds-v1 ground truth. This fixture owns confirmation sampling and maintained statistical/method policy only; it does not restate world relationships, targets, dimensions, or identifiability semantics.

dimension_selector.interpretation_boundary: The TWO-NN likelihood selects intrinsic dimensions for each observed view and their concatenated joint sample without ground-truth access. Shared/private dimensions are then derived only by the declared additive dimension identity for this structural-world benchmark; the result is not a universal topology claim for climate data.

evaluation_policy.coordinate_recovery_metric: absolute Spearman rank correlation with the authoritative shared_evaluation_target_name when one exists
evaluation_policy.abstention_policy: A world with no authoritative shared evaluation target expects abstention. A world with an authoritative shared evaluation target expects the dependence selector to support a shared coordinate. No per-world labels are restated here.
evaluation_policy.confirmation_policy: Confirmation worlds use the same authoritative world semantics and sample count with each base seed increased by confirmation_seed_offset. Method settings and selector alpha are fixed before confirmation execution.
evaluation_policy.failure_policy: A coordinate baseline failure is recorded as a method failure for that world rather than silently substituted by another algorithm.
evaluation_policy.matched_information_policy: For worlds with an authoritative shared evaluation target, fit the same k-nearest-neighbor regressor on discovery targets for each listed representation and score only on confirmation targets. Raw/PCA/CCA/factor representations are fit from discovery views without target access; the downstream target probe is identical across representations. Spectral and JSF remain separate held-out coordinate diagnostics because these registered implementations do not expose the same maintained out-of-sample transform contract.
